newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian arms agency proud of success against U.S..
newsitem.headline: Russian arms agency proud of success against U.S..

text.p: The head of Moscow's state arms export agency said on Sunday he considered Russia's sale of 10 military transport helicopters to Colombia a great success against United States competition.
"To strike such a deal in the underbelly of our rivals, under such pressure..We are very proud of it," said General Alexander Kotyolkin, head of the Rossvorozhenia agency.

Russia's arms sales dropped off dramatically after the collapse of the Soviet Union and the captive Warsaw Pact market. But in the last couple of years, Moscow has sought out new markets and boosted its share of the world market again.

Colombia agreed last month to buy about 10 Mi-17 transport helicopters, though U.S. officials have expressed disapproval of the deal. Russia believes the United States and other Western governments are trying to keep Russia out of their traditional markets by exerting political pressure.
General Kotyolkin told Russian Television's Zerkalo (Mirror) programme also that Russia planned to go ahead with another controversial deal to sell S300 anti-aircraft defence systems to Cyprus.

The Cypriot government's decision to buy the missiles has heightened tensions with the Turkish-occupied north of the island. But Russia insists the S300s do not upset the power balance existing since the 1974 Turkish occupation.
"The contract will be implemented on time. This is the position of the Russian government. this is also the decision of the Cyprus government," Kotyolkin said.
